root.name: Italian Game: Anti-Fried Liver Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 h6

overview: Black spends a tempo on ...h6 to rule out Ng5 and the Fried Liver after ...Nf6. White can play c3 and d4 or d3 and O-O and get a free development advantage. I know this only as a rare waiting move; I am reasoning from the moves rather than from detailed theory.

white_ideas.idea: c3, d4 or d3 and O-O, using the extra tempo for development and central space
Keep options of Ng5-free attacks like d4 and Bg5 pins

black_ideas.idea: Follow with ...Nf6, ...Bc5, ...d6 and ...O-O in a solid Italian

typical_structures.structure: Giuoco Piano/Pianissimo-type with ...h6 played, e4/d3 against e5/d6

character.notes: Quiet, ...h6 slows Black, no real tactics.

soundness.notes: Playable but loses a tempo; not refuted.

approach.notes: A rare waiting move that strong players seldom choose.

character.reason: Quiet position with no sharp theory and no solid-wall reputation.

soundness.reason: Loses a tempo but not refuted.

approach.reason: A rarely chosen move order for strong players.
